title: history you shaped on purpose
goal: C1 Interactive rebase: squash, reword, split, drop
startWith: In git-lab, make five sloppy commits (“wip”, “fix”, “typo”) and clean them into two honest ones.

newIdeas.plain: Replay a list of commits, deciding for each one: keep, reword, squash, edit, drop.
Mark a commit as “belongs to that one” and let rebase fold it in automatically.
Rewrite only history nobody else has pulled.

tasks.do: Make five throwaway commits, then rebase them interactively

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do echo $i >> notes.txt; git add -A; git commit -m "wip $i"; done
git rebase -i HEAD~5
# in the editor: pick / reword / squash / fixup / drop. Top line is the oldest commit.

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: Log tab → right-click a commit → Interactively Rebase from Here. A real dialog instead of an editor full of comments — the friendliest interactive rebase there is.

tasks.do: Amend the previous commit, with and without changing the message

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: The Commit dialog has an Amend checkbox; ticking it loads the last message.

tasks.do: Use fixup and autosquash for a review comment
tasks.why: A reviewer says “line 12 is wrong” three commits back. This puts the fix where it belongs with no manual reordering.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git add -p
git commit --fixup=<hash-of-the-commit-it-fixes>
git rebase -i --autosquash <hash>~1
git config --global rebase.autosquash true    # make it the default

tasks.do: Stage part of a file with add -p
tasks.why: Two unrelated changes in one file should be two commits. This is how.

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body: git add -p        # y / n / s to split the hunk / e to edit it

blocks.label: IntelliJ
blocks.body: In the Commit dialog's diff, select lines and right-click → Include into commit. Per-line staging with a mouse.

tasks.do: Rebase your branch onto an updated main, then push it safely

blocks.label: terminal
blocks.body:
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/main
# resolve conflicts, then one of:
git rebase --continue
git rebase --skip
git rebase --abort
git push --force-with-lease

proof.note: Five wip commits became a history you would show someone.

doneWhen: Your branch arrives at review as a readable sequence, not a diary.

lessons.title: Interactively rebase from a commit
lessons.teach: In the Log, right-click a commit → Interactively Rebase from Here. Squash, reword, drop and reorder in a dialog with the diffs beside it — the same rebase, without the editor full of comment lines.
